note: The high-plain deity 'gives birth to' / commands the birth of Izanagi.
explanation: The Kojiki words this as the kami of the high plain 'giving birth to' the pair and ordering them to shape the islands; the Nihon Shoki phrases it as a command. Whether 'birth' is literal or a ritual/creative order is debated.

note: The high-plain deity 'gives birth to' / commands the birth of Izanami.
explanation: As with Izanagi: the Kojiki's 'birth' of the creator pair from the high plain vs. the Nihon Shoki's 'command.'

Amaterasu is estranged from Tsukuyomi after he desecrates the weaving hall (the mythic separation of sun and moon).
explanation: This is a mythic 'estrangement' (the separate courses of sun and moon), not a battle. The Kojiki's Ukehimuka episode is the stated cause; wording differs in the Nihon Shoki.

note: Amaterasu and Susanoo are estranged after his violent misconduct; he is banished from heaven.
explanation: A mythic estrangement/banishment rather than a battle. The list of his 'transgressions' (fields, weaving hall) differs slightly between the texts.

note: Susanoo slays the eight-headed serpent Yamata-no-Orochi.
Susanoo marries the rescued Kushinada-hime.
Kushinada-hime marries Susanoo (symmetric).
The fire of Kagutsuchi's birth burns and kills his mother Izanami.
explanation: The Kojiki states that in giving birth to the fire god, Izanami 'was burned and died.' The 'killing' is the fire of childbirth, not a deliberate act.

note: Amaterasu is the parent of the heavenly bride Toyotama-hime.
Ninigi is Amaterasu's grandson, the sent-down heavenly prince.
explanation: The Kojiki makes Ninigi the grandson of Amaterasu (through the line); the precise generational link (Toyotama-hime as the intermediate) is stated in the descent episode.

note: Ninigi marries the earthly bride Konohanasakuya-hime.
Ninigi marries the heavenly bride Toyotama-hime.
Ninigi (with Toyotama-hime) is the parent of Hooroni, the imperial ancestor.
Toyotama-hime (with Ninigi) is the parent of Hooroni.
Ōkuninushi is the parent of the flower goddess Konohanasakuya-hime.
explanation: Some accounts make her a daughter of Ōkuninushi; others a local mountain deity. The Kojiki/Nihon Shoki differ on the exact parentage.

note: Takemikazuchi throws the sword in the contest against Ōkuninushi's side.
explanation: The 'contest' (the sword-throw) is the Kuniyurinshi; the sequence of acts differs between the Kojiki and Nihon Shoki.

note: Susanoo takes part in the subjugation of Ōkuninushi (Kuniyurinshi).
Ninigi's heavenly side confronts Ōkuninushi in the Kuniyurinshi.
Sarutahiko guides Ninigi and is subdued in the contest.
Sarutahiko leads Ōkuninushi's retinue.
Kotohikone brokers the alliance/marriage in the handover.
The heavenly line (Ninigi) succeeds to rule the land that Ōkuninushi held.
explanation: The 'succession' is the transfer of sovereignty in the Kuniyurinshi; Ōkuninushi becomes a local deity thereafter.

note: Ōkuninushi rules the middle land (until the Kuniyurinshi).
Ame-no-Uzume's dance lures Amaterasu out of the cave.
Takemikazuchi's clamor helps draw Amaterasu out.
